title: Excretory system
summary: How does the body get rid of waste and keep its internal balance?
cards.0.p: Metabolism constantly makes waste. This waste is CO2, nitrogenous waste, extra water and salt. Excretion removes this waste and keeps the water, salt and pH balance of the blood. This balance is called homeostasis.
cards.0.svg#0: waste: CO₂, nitrogenous waste, extra water and salt
cards.0.svg#9: values are kept in a narrow range: homeostasis
cards.0.key: Excretion is not just removing waste. Adjusting the makeup of the blood is also its job.
cards.0.once.soru: When you drink a lot of water, you urinate more. Why does the kidney remove the extra water?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: The water and salt levels of the blood are kept within narrow limits. Any excess is removed.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Water is not harmful. Only an excess upsets the balance.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: The bladder only stores urine. How much water to remove depends on the balance of the blood.
cards.1.p: When amino acids are broken down, toxic ammonia forms, and a lot of water is needed to dilute it. Living things turn ammonia into less toxic urea or uric acid. This conversion takes energy.
cards.1.svg#19: ammonia → urea → uric acid: more water saved
cards.1.key: Ammonia is the most toxic waste and needs the most water, followed by urea and uric acid. The energy cost of making these wastes runs in the opposite order.
cards.1.once.soru: When proteins are broken down, which waste forms that does not form from carbohydrates?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: The amino group in amino acids carries nitrogen. When amino acids are broken down, ammonia forms from this group.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: CO₂ and water also form when carbohydrates and fats are broken down. Protein breakdown makes nitrogenous waste on top of these.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: Glucose is a fuel, not a waste.
cards.2.h: Life in water, life on land
cards.2.p: The type of waste an animal gets rid of depends on how much water it has access to. Most bony fish excrete ammonia, and mammals excrete urea. Birds, most reptiles and insects excrete uric acid.
cards.2.key: Adult frogs also excrete urea. Tadpoles, which live in water, excrete ammonia.
cards.3.h: Urea is made in the liver
cards.3.p: The liver combines ammonia with CO2 and turns it into urea. This process is called the ornithine cycle, and it uses ATP. Urea passes into the blood and is filtered in the kidney. So the kidney does not make urea, it only removes it.
cards.3.svg#10: urea is made in the liver and removed by the kidney
cards.3.key: In liver failure, ammonia cannot be turned into urea. Ammonia builds up in the blood and affects the brain.
cards.4.p: The lungs remove CO2 and water vapor, and the skin removes water and salt in sweat. The liver adds pigments to bile. The large intestine removes these pigments and some minerals from the body.
cards.4.key: Bile pigments come from broken-down red blood cells. Getting rid of undigested food is not excretion, it is defecation.
cards.4.once.soru: Besides the kidney, which organ also carries out excretion?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: The lungs remove CO₂ and water vapor from the blood.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: The stomach digests food. It does not excrete.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: The heart pumps blood. It does not remove waste.
cards.5.p: Urine forms in the kidney, flows down the ureter to the bladder and collects there. When the bladder is full, urine leaves through the urethra. The internal sphincter is involuntary, and the external sphincter is voluntary.
cards.5.key: The kidneys sit on either side of the lower back. Two ureters run from the kidneys to the bladder. There is only one urethra leading out of the bladder.
cards.5.once.soru: You can hold in your urine for a while. What makes this possible?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: The external sphincter at the bladder's exit is voluntary, and you contract it yourself.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: The kidney keeps making urine, and it collects in the bladder.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder. The bladder's exit is closed by a sphincter.
cards.6.p: The outer part of the kidney is called the cortex, and the middle part is the medulla. In the inner part is the renal pelvis, where urine collects. Each kidney has about a million filtering units called nephrons.
cards.6.key: The glomerulus and Bowman's capsule are in the cortex, and the loop of Henle is in the medulla. Urine leaves the renal pelvis through the ureter.
cards.6.once.soru: About how many filtering units does one kidney have?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: Each kidney has about a million nephrons.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: The real number is much larger. The kidney filters blood in a very large number of tiny units.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: The real number is about a thousand times larger.
cards.7.h: The nephron: the kidney's filtering unit
cards.7.p: Blood comes to a ball of capillaries called the glomerulus, and Bowman's capsule collects the filtrate. The filtrate passes through the proximal tubule, the loop of Henle, the distal tubule and the collecting duct, in that order.
cards.7.key: Many nephrons open into one shared collecting duct. Urine flows from there into the renal pelvis.
cards.7.etk.soru: Tap the parts of the nephron and follow the path of the filtrate.
cards.7.etk.noktalar.0.acik: The glomerulus is a ball of capillaries. The high blood pressure here filters part of the plasma into the capsule.
cards.7.etk.noktalar.1.acik: Bowman's capsule wraps the glomerulus like a cup. It collects the filtrate and sends it into the tubule.
cards.7.etk.noktalar.2.acik: All of the glucose and amino acids, and most of the water and Na<sup>+</sup>, are reabsorbed into the blood here.
cards.7.etk.noktalar.3.acik: The loop of Henle is a U-shaped bend that reaches into the medulla. It helps concentrate the urine by allowing water and salt to be reabsorbed.
cards.7.etk.noktalar.4.acik: Secretion happens in the distal tubule, and Na<sup>+</sup> reabsorption continues under the effect of aldosterone.
cards.7.etk.noktalar.5.acik: The collecting duct is shared by many nephrons. ADH increases water reabsorption here.
cards.7.once.soru: Where is blood first filtered in the kidney?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: This ball of capillaries is called the glomerulus. Plasma filters from here into the capsule.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: The bladder only stores urine. Filtering happens in the kidney.
cards.8.p: The high pressure in the glomerulus pushes plasma into the capsule. Water, glucose, amino acids, salt and urea pass into the capsule. Blood cells and large proteins do not. No ATP is used in this filtration.
cards.8.svg#5: driving force: blood pressure (no ATP used)
cards.8.key: The vessel that brings blood to the glomerulus is wider than the one that takes it away, and this creates the pressure. About 180 L of filtrate forms each day. After heavy bleeding, the pressure drops and filtration decreases.
cards.9.p: Useful substances return from the tubules to the blood. All of the glucose and amino acids, and most of the water and Na+, are reabsorbed. Most reabsorption happens in the proximal tubule, and about 99% of the filtrate returns to the blood.
cards.9.svg#10: tubule to blood · mostly in the proximal tubule
cards.9.svg#11: 180 L of filtrate → about 1.8 L of urine
cards.9.key: Glucose, amino acids and Na⁺ cross by active transport, and water by osmosis. Reabsorption goes from tubule to blood, and secretion goes from blood to tubule.
cards.10.p: In secretion, H+, K+, ammonia and some drugs are moved from the blood into the tubule. When the blood becomes acidic, more H+ is secreted. This keeps the blood pH at about 7.4.
cards.10.svg#1: nephron tubule (fluid that will become urine)
cards.10.svg#6: more H⁺ is secreted when the blood is acidic
cards.10.key: While H⁺ is secreted, HCO₃⁻ is reabsorbed at the same time. Secretion also adds substances that stayed in the blood after filtration to the urine.
cards.11.h: The loop of Henle and concentrated urine
cards.11.p: The ascending limb of the loop of Henle releases salt into the medulla, but does not let water through. So the medulla gets saltier the deeper you go. Water leaves the descending limb and the collecting duct by osmosis, and the urine becomes concentrated.
cards.11.svg#10: the ascending limb blocks water and releases salt into the medulla
cards.11.key: The flow in the two limbs runs in opposite directions, which is called countercurrent flow. Water leaves the collecting duct only when ADH is present.
cards.11.once.soru: The kangaroo rat lives in the desert and almost never drinks water. Which part of its kidney is very long?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: A long loop of Henle makes the medulla very salty. So water is recovered and the urine is very concentrated.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: The ureter only carries urine. It does not recover water.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: The bladder stores urine, but it does not set how concentrated the urine is.
cards.12.p: When you drink little water, the pituitary releases ADH. The collecting duct reabsorbs more water and urine decreases. When blood pressure drops, aldosterone increases Na+ reabsorption in the distal tubule.
cards.12.key: ADH is made in the hypothalamus. Aldosterone release is triggered by renin, which the kidney releases. Alcohol suppresses ADH, so urine increases.
cards.13.h: How does blood change as it passes through the kidney?
cards.13.p: In the blood leaving the kidney, urea has dropped, and water and salt are balanced. Because kidney cells carry out respiration, O<sub>2</sub> and glucose drop in this blood and CO<sub>2</sub> rises.
cards.13.svg#11: blood leaving the glomerulus is still oxygenated
cards.13.svg#12: it drops its O₂ in the capillaries around the tubules
cards.13.key: Blood leaving the glomerulus is still oxygenated. The blood with the least urea is in the renal vein, and the blood with the most urea is in the hepatic vein.
cards.13.once.soru: Compared with the renal artery, what has decreased in the blood of the renal vein?
cards.13.once.secenekler.0.neden: Urea is filtered and removed in the urine.
cards.13.once.secenekler.1.neden: Kidney cells carry out respiration, so CO₂ increases.
cards.13.once.secenekler.2.neden: Red blood cells are not filtered, so their number does not change.
cards.14.p: Drinking too little water can lead to kidney stones. If the kidneys fail, urea and K+ build up in the blood. Then the blood is cleaned by dialysis, or a kidney transplant is done.
cards.14.svg#0: dialysis: diffusion through a semipermeable membrane
cards.14.svg#5: blood cells and proteins do not cross the membrane
cards.14.svg#6: the fluid has no urea, so urea moves from blood into the fluid
cards.14.key: In dialysis, urea and extra salt cross the membrane. Blood cells and proteins do not.
cards.14.once.soru: A dialysis machine passes blood across a semipermeable membrane. What must not cross the membrane?
cards.14.once.secenekler.0.neden: Blood cells and proteins must stay in the blood. That is why the membrane does not let them through.
cards.14.once.secenekler.1.neden: Urea crosses the membrane, because the goal of dialysis is to remove urea.
cards.14.once.secenekler.2.neden: Extra salt also crosses the membrane and is removed.
cards.15.p:
• Excretion keeps the internal balance, that is, homeostasis.
• Ammonia is the main waste in aquatic animals, urea in mammals and uric acid in birds and insects. Urea is made in the liver.
• In the nephron, urine forms through filtration, reabsorption and secretion.
• ADH increases water reabsorption, and aldosterone increases Na+ reabsorption.
• Urine follows the path kidney, ureter, bladder, urethra.
quiz.0.q: A person forms 180 L of filtrate a day, and 98.5% of the filtrate is reabsorbed. How many liters of urine form per day?
quiz.0.e: The part not reabsorbed is 1.5%. 180 × 0.015 = 2.7 L. A small drop in the reabsorption percentage greatly increases the amount of urine.
quiz.1.q: Starting where blood is filtered, put in order the path the filtrate takes through the nephron.
quiz.1.e: Plasma is filtered from the glomerulus into Bowman's capsule. The filtrate passes through the proximal tubule, the loop of Henle and the distal tubule and opens into the collecting duct. Urine flows from there into the renal pelvis.
quiz.2.q: Which of these are found in a healthy person's urine? Put each one in the right group.
quiz.2.e: Urea is filtered and removed. H<sup>+</sup> and ammonia are secreted into the tubule. All of the glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed. Red blood cells and large proteins are never filtered in the glomerulus.
quiz.3.q: After heavy bleeding, a person's blood pressure drops. What is expected in the kidney?
quiz.3.o.0: Renin drops and Na⁺ excretion rises.
quiz.3.o.1: Renin and aldosterone rise, and Na⁺ and water are reabsorbed.
quiz.3.o.2: ADH drops and urine becomes plentiful.
quiz.3.o.3: Filtration in the glomerulus speeds up and urine increases.
quiz.3.e: When blood pressure drops, the kidney releases renin, and at the end of the chain aldosterone rises. Na⁺ is reabsorbed in the distal tubule, and water follows it. This protects blood volume.
quiz.3.y.0: When pressure drops, the kidney does not lower renin, it raises it. The goal is to keep Na⁺ and water.
quiz.3.y.2: After blood loss, ADH rises and water is kept. So urine decreases.
quiz.3.y.3: When blood pressure drops, filtration in the glomerulus decreases, not increases.
A:ozet: Compare nitrogenous wastes, follow the path of urea, filter in the nephron, reabsorb, and keep the blood's pH and water in balance.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Compare the three wastes. Then think about an embryo inside a shelled egg.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.soru: An embryo in a shelled egg stores its waste inside the egg. Which waste suits this?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Ammonia is very toxic and needs a lot of water to dilute it. If it built up in a closed egg, it would poison the embryo.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Urea dissolves in water, and as it builds up it still needs water. A closed egg does not have that much water.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Uric acid is barely toxic and forms crystals that do not dissolve in water. So it needs almost no water. Bird and reptile embryos store their waste this way.
A:adimlar.1.metin: When extra amino acids are broken down, ammonia forms. One organ combines ammonia with CO₂ to make urea, and another organ filters urea out of the blood. Make a guess first, then watch.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: In which organ is urea made?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The kidney does not make urea. It filters urea out of the blood and removes it in urine.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Ammonia combines with CO₂ in the liver. The urea that forms is carried by the blood to the kidney.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The bladder only stores urine, and no urea is made in it.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Blood pressure pushes plasma from the glomerulus into Bowman's capsule. Make a guess first, then press play.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: Which ones do not pass into Bowman's capsule?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Blood cells and large proteins are too big to pass through the filtering membrane. The filtrate is like plasma without them.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Glucose and amino acids are small, so they are filtered. Later they are reabsorbed into the blood in the tubules.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Urea and salts are small, so they pass into the filtrate. Most urea is removed in urine.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Your two kidneys form about 180 L of filtrate a day, but you make only about 1.8 L of urine a day. Useful substances and most of the water return from the tubules to the blood. Adjust the reabsorption.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.ipucu: What percentage of 180 L is 1.8 L of urine a day? The rest returns to the blood.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: 99% of the 180 L of filtrate returned to the blood, and only 1.8 L of urine was left.
A:adimlar.4.metin: The blood has become acidic and its pH has dropped to 7.22. The kidney can secrete H⁺ from the blood into the tubule. Make the kidney secrete H⁺ and bring the pH back to normal.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.ipucu: Normal blood pH is between 7.35 and 7.45. If you secrete too much, the blood becomes basic.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: After 3 units of H⁺ were secreted, the blood pH returned to 7.4.
A:adimlar.5.metin: How much water the collecting duct reabsorbs is set by ADH, which the pituitary releases. Compare the three situations.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: What happens in someone who sweats a lot and drinks little water?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: ADH drops, urine is plentiful and pale
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: This happens when you drink a lot of water. When you sweat, the blood becomes concentrated and the body tries to keep water.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.yazi: ADH rises, urine is scant and dark
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: When the blood becomes concentrated, ADH rises and the collecting duct reabsorbs more water. Urine decreases and gets darker.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Filtration in the glomerulus continues. What changes is how much water is reabsorbed in the collecting duct.
A:adimlar.6.metin: Glucose is reabsorbed by carriers in the proximal tubule. The number of carriers is limited. Raise the blood sugar and find the value at which glucose first appears in the urine.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.ipucu: Until the carriers are full, all the glucose returns to the blood. Stop at the value where glucose first leaks into the urine.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: Up to a blood sugar of about 180 mg/dL, all the glucose is reabsorbed. Above this value the carriers are full and the extra glucose leaks into the urine. Glucose in the urine is usually a sign of diabetes.
A:kapanis.0: Ammonia is the main waste in aquatic animals, urea in mammals, and uric acid in birds, reptiles and insects.
A:kapanis.1: Urea is made in the liver and removed by the kidney. Urine passes through the ureter, bladder and urethra.
A:kapanis.2: In the glomerulus, all of the plasma except red cells and large proteins is filtered. 99% of the filtrate is reabsorbed.
A:kapanis.3: Secretion goes from blood to tubule. By secreting H⁺ and reabsorbing HCO₃⁻, the kidney keeps the blood pH at 7.4.
A:kapanis.4: ADH increases water reabsorption in the collecting duct. When the glucose carriers are saturated, glucose passes into the urine.
